title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Tamboran Persons
tiers.description: All Directors and Senior Management (each director, the CEO, CFO, Managing Director and Company Secretary, and Key Management Personnel) and any other person the Board designates in writing, plus companies or trusts they control and, for certain purposes, their spouse, child, close relative or a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with them. All substantive prohibitions (blackout periods, no speculative trading, no protection arrangements, no granting of security or margin lending) apply to this tier without differentiation; tiers below are distinguished only for the identity of the Authorising Officer.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: authorised by the chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Other directors, Company Secretary and KMP
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: authorised by the chair of the Board or, in his/her absence, the chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Any other Tamboran Person
tiers.description: Any Tamboran Person other than a director, the Company Secretary or KMP; distinguished only for clearance: authorised by the Company Secretary or, in his/her absence, the CEO.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A company or trust controlled by a Tamboran Person, and (for the purposes of the definition of Directors and Senior Management) a spouse, child, close relative or person financially dependent on or acting in concert with a Tamboran Person.

definitions.hedging_definition: operate to limit the economic risk of any Tamboran Person’s security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Tamboran’s securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under any Tamboran incentive plan) on that Tamboran Person’s behalf

windows.end_anchor: after the release of the Company's quarterly report

windows.start_anchor: four weeks immediately preceding the release of the Company's half-year report
windows.end_anchor: after the release of the Company's half-year report

windows.start_anchor: four weeks immediately preceding the release of the Company's full-year report
windows.end_anchor: after the release of the Company's full-year report

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other period as a Blackout Period from time to time (1.5(a)(iv)). The policy does not state whether such additional blackout periods are announced or kept confidential.

rules.detail: Protection arrangements over any Tamboran securities or Tamboran products in the derivatives markets are banned outright while the underlying securities are unvested.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of “protection arrangements” for any Tamboran securities (or Tamboran products in the derivatives markets): (a) is prohibited at any time in respect of any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Same absolute ban extends to vested securities still subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Once vested and unrestricted, a protection arrangement (which includes derivatives over the securities) requires prior consent from the Authorising Officer under 1.6.
rules.evidence: otherwise, requires consent under paragraph 1.6.

rules.detail: Hedging arrangements are given as an express example of a banned protection arrangement over unvested securities.
rules.evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of any Tamboran Person’s security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Tamboran’s securities held beneficially ... is prohibited at any time in respect of any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Same ban extends to vested but holding-locked securities.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Hedging of vested, unrestricted securities requires prior consent under 1.6.
rules.evidence: otherwise, requires consent under paragraph 1.6.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a structure that lets the holder profit from a price decrease or otherwise limits economic risk falls within 'protection arrangements', banned outright while unvested.
rules.evidence: otherwise enable a Tamboran Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.

rules.detail: Same ban extends to vested but holding-locked securities.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: A monetisation structure over vested, unrestricted securities is caught as a protection arrangement and requires consent under 1.6.
rules.evidence: otherwise, requires consent under paragraph 1.6.

rules.detail: Short selling beyond the person's holding is a named example of a protection arrangement, banned outright over unvested securities.
rules.evidence: amount to “short selling” of securities beyond the Tamboran Person’s holding of securities

rules.detail: Same ban extends to vested but holding-locked securities.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Short selling beyond holding, once the relevant securities are vested and unrestricted, requires consent under 1.6.
rules.evidence: otherwise, requires consent under paragraph 1.6.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy and is not listed among the protection-arrangement examples.

Contracts for difference are named as an example of derivative-market transactions caught by the no speculative/short-term trading ban; a CFD used to limit economic risk would separately be caught as a protection arrangement under 1.10.
rules.evidence: transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative

rules.detail: Margin lending arrangements involving unvested or holding-locked Tamboran securities are banned outright.
rules.evidence: Tamboran Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock ... or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Tamboran securities.

rules.detail: Same ban extends to vested but holding-locked securities.
rules.evidence: over any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock ... or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Tamboran securities.

rules.detail: Once vested and unrestricted, a margin lending arrangement requires prior consent under 1.6.
rules.evidence: Unless paragraph (a) applies, Tamboran Persons may, directly or indirectly, ... enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Tamboran securities, with consent under paragraph 1.6.

rules.detail: Granting any form of security over unvested or holding-locked Tamboran securities, to secure any obligation of the person or a third party, is banned outright.
rules.evidence: Tamboran Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Tamboran Person or any third party

rules.detail: Same ban extends to vested but holding-locked securities.
rules.evidence: over any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Tamboran Person or any third party

rules.detail: Granting security over vested, unrestricted securities is permitted with prior consent under 1.6.
rules.evidence: Unless paragraph (a) applies, Tamboran Persons may, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... to secure any obligation of that Tamboran Person or any third party ... with consent under paragraph 1.6.

rules.detail: Any secured financing arrangement (grant of security to secure any obligation, or margin lending) over unvested or holding-locked securities is banned outright.
rules.evidence: grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Tamboran Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Same ban extends to vested but holding-locked securities.
rules.evidence: over any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Tamboran Person or any third party

rules.detail: A secured financing arrangement (a bank loan secured against the collared shares) over vested, unrestricted securities is permitted with prior consent under 1.6.
rules.evidence: Unless paragraph (a) applies, Tamboran Persons may, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... to secure any obligation of that Tamboran Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Tamboran securities, with consent under paragraph 1.6.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on short-term or speculative trading, including short-term direct dealing and short-term or speculative derivative transactions; no defined holding period is stated.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should Tamboran Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Tamboran securities.

exceptions.evidence: may include, without limitation, severe financial hardship
or a requirement to comply with a court order or court enforceable undertaking.
trade Tamboran securities where the trading does not result in a change of beneficial interest in the securities

acquire securities under any director or employee security plan or through the exercise of options or performance rights under an option or performance rights plan or acquire, or agree to acquire, options or performance rights
transfer Tamboran securities already held into a self-managed superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the restricted person is a beneficiary
acquire Tamboran’s ordinary shares by conversion of securities giving a right of conversion to Tamboran’s ordinary shares
acquire Tamboran’s securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer

invest in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of Tamboran) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party
a disposal of Tamboran securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement

where a restricted person is a trustee, trade in the securities managed by that trust provided the restricted person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently

trade under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan or an equal access buy-back
trade during a Permitted Trading Window.

exemption_authority: The Authorising Officer, in the Board's absolute discretion, may approve dealing during a Blackout Period or other otherwise-prohibited dealing in 'exceptional circumstances' such as severe financial hardship or a court order/enforceable undertaking; approval must be given by email and notification requirements still apply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Tamboran securities (or Tamboran products in the derivatives markets) ... includes ... operate to limit the economic risk of any Tamboran Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) ... or otherwise enable a Tamboran Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC put and call over vested, unrestricted shares squarely falls within 'protection arrangements' and is permitted only with prior consent under 1.6; over unvested or holding-locked shares it is banned outright.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Tamboran securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of collared shares under the loan security is an exempted dealing that Tamboran Persons may make at any time, including during a Blackout Period, subject only to advising the Authorising Officer per 1.12(b) — a clean lender remedy.

bespoke_clauses.topic: granting security ban on unvested/locked shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: Tamboran Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Tamboran securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Tamboran Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Tamboran securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's loan cannot be secured on shares before vesting or while subject to a holding lock, so the funded collar can only be structured over vested, unrestricted shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: consent for security/margin over vested shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: Unless paragraph (a) applies, Tamboran Persons may, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Tamboran securities, with consent under paragraph 1.6.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of the collar, secured on vested unrestricted shares, is permitted but needs prior written consent from the relevant Authorising Officer, the same as the derivative legs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy uses 'buy or sell', 'trade' and 'deal in' without one omnibus defined term for 'Dealing' (contrast a typical Attachment-style definition).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Activities are expressly and separately named (protection arrangements at 1.10, security/margin lending at 1.11) rather than swept in by a broad dealing definition, which reduces ambiguity about whether a bespoke OTC collar or its financing leg is caught — both are caught expressly.

bespoke_clauses.clause: for the purposes of section (d) only, a spouse (including a de facto spouse), child ... a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with any of the persons referred to in sub-paragraph (i)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The associate extension is literally limited to 'section (d)' (the Directors and Senior Management definition); a bank should not rely on this apparent gap to route a collar or loan through an associate's account, as the Company would likely treat it as caught regardless.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances the Authorising Officer, has discretion to approve dealings in Tamboran securities during a Blackout Period, or other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into or unwind of a collar during a Blackout Period is not a right but could be approved case-by-case for hardship or court order, via email, at the Board's absolute discretion.

summary: A funded collar is not possible over unvested or holding-locked Tamboran shares: protection arrangements (which expressly include hedging and short-selling-type instruments) and any grant of security or margin lending over such shares are banned outright under 1.10(a) and 1.11(a). Over vested, unrestricted shares, both the derivative legs (as a 'protection arrangement') and the secured loan leg (as a grant of security or margin lending arrangement) are permitted, but each requires prior written-style consent from the applicable Authorising Officer (chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Board chair; the Board chair for other directors, Company Secretary and KMP; the Company Secretary or CEO for others), confirmation of no inside information, a post-trade transaction confirmation, and must sit outside Blackout Periods unless the Board exercises its narrow 'exceptional circumstances' discretion. The document usefully exempts a secured lender's forced sale on default from the Blackout/dealing restrictions, so the bank's enforcement remedy is not itself blocked, though the executive must still notify the Authorising Officer. Tenor and structuring should avoid characterisation as 'short-term or speculative trading', which is banned outright with no defined holding period. Overall: workable over vested unrestricted shares with prior consent at each stage, but entirely blocked while shares remain unvested or holding-locked.
